newsitem.title: UK: Pressure on lead seen continuing after chart break.
newsitem.headline: Pressure on lead seen continuing after chart break.

text.p: Investment fund liquidation against a backdrop of deteriorating charts is likely to keep London Metal Exchange (LME) lead prices under pressure in the near term, traders said.
On Tuesday three months delivery lead fell to a 10-month low of $693, down from Monday's close of $717.50 and registered a near 20 percent loss from its 1996 zenith of $861.
Traders said the move was largely chart driven after prices breached a long term uptrend line and expected psychological support at $700.
The uptrend line joined a string of lows extending back to October 1993, traders and analysts added.

They expected the chart pressure to continue and did not rule out a test of key trend support at $675. "The charts have been eroded from beneath the market but fresh demand is bound to rally the market once the chart pressure has run its course," one trader said.
Cold weather could spark demand from the replacement battery industry during the Northern hemisphere winter months.
"I would expect trade buying to grow over the coming weeks, although there are few signs that they are coivering at the moment," one LME floor trader commented. --London Newsroom +44 71 510 8075
